title: How do you connect direct mail to email, SMS, and paid ads?
summary: Your existing data can power your direct mail the same way it drives email and SMS. Here’s how to connect mail to your digital channels for a fully coordinated customer journey.
body_markdown:
You already use email, SMS, and paid ads. Maybe they’re even working together through a CRM or CDP. But if direct mail isn’t part of your journeys, you may be missing out on engagement. According to Lob’s[State of Direct Mail Consumer Insights 2026](https://www.lob.com/state-of-direct-mail/consumer-insights/2026-report) report, 41% of consumers say they’re more likely to engage when they receive both mail and digital touchpoints together.


Here’s how to bring mail into the mix as a fully integrated channel.


## Start with your data infrastructure


Your existing customer data – the same behavior data that powers your email triggers, your SMS sends, and your paid ad audiences – can drive your direct mail too. Through APIs or turnkey integrations with platforms like Braze, Salesforce, or HubSpot, mail becomes another channel in the same workflow rather than a separate program to manage.


And the data can flow both ways. Look for mail platforms that send[tracking data](https://www.lob.com/blog/what-do-usps-tracking-scan-events-actually-mean) back to your CRM, so delivery events, response signals, and attribution data live alongside the rest of your customer activity and can be used to fire other parts of your campaigns, such as emails or texts.


## Add in addresses


The most integrated programs also append physical addresses to digital records, so prospects and customers they’d otherwise only reach digitally become accessible by mail.


SimpliSafe, this year’s[Postmark Award winner for Top Omnichannel Integration](https://www.lob.com/postmark-awards/top-omnichannel-integration) , reached a match rate as high as 90% by appending addresses to digital leads, turning a digital-only audience into a cross-channel one.


## Trigger mail from digital behavior


Once your data is integrated, a new lead, abandoned cart, lapsed purchase pattern, or a product launch similar to a past purchase can all set off a mailpiece at exactly the right moment.


You can also trigger mail off of interactions, or lack of engagement, with other channels throughout the customer lifecycle. Did a prospect click on an ad? Fire off a special offer acquisition postcard to amplify your digital message. Did a once active customer stop opening emails? Plug the communication gap with a personalized self-mailer.


## Sequence channels deliberately


[Timing between channels](https://www.lob.com/blog/what-is-the-right-cadence-for-a-direct-mail-campaign) matters as much as which channels you use. A postcard that arrives the same week as an email reinforces the message from two directions. A mail piece that drops before a digital campaign builds awareness before the digital push lands, and can even act as a fridge-worthy save the date for enrollment deadlines and promotions. A follow-up SMS after mail delivers gives recipients a frictionless path to act.


Pro tip: Map your channel sequence around your in-home date, not your send date. Knowing when mail arrives lets you time digital touchpoints to land at the right moment in the customer’s experience.


## Use mail to reach who digital misses


Email open rates vary. Paid social audiences have gaps. Direct mail reaches people regardless of inbox behavior or algorithm changes, making it a reliable way to fill coverage gaps in a digital-first program.


For prospects who haven’t engaged digitally, a physical mailpiece can open the door. For customers who’ve gone quiet across digital channels, mail often reactivates them when nothing else does. According to the Consumer Insights report, 83% of consumers say direct mail would influence them to re-engage with a brand they haven’t interacted with recently.
